title: Heterogenization of molecular catalysts in MOFs and COFs: Re-bipyridine CO 2  reduction systems as a model platform
content: The rise in atmospheric CO2 concentrations and the growing global demand for sustainable energy have intensified research into approaches that combine carbon utilisation with the conversion of renewable energy. CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) using solar energy offers a promising avenue in this context. A wide range of molecular CO2RR catalysts has been developed and extensively investigated, offering high selectivity and productivity together with tunable electronic structures and well-defined catalytic mechanisms. Among these, the fac-[ReI(bpy-R)(CO)X] family (bpy-R = 2,2′-bipyridine derivative; X = Cl or Br) has long served as a benchmark platform for photo- and electrocatalytic CO2RR due to its high yield, excellent selectivity towards CO and well-defined catalytic mechanisms. However, the homogeneous nature of these catalysts can lead to deactivation, poor recyclability, inefficient light harvesting and limited long-term stability. The integration of Re-bpy catalysts into porous crystalline materials, in particular metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (COFs), offers a strategy for combining molecular-level catalytic precision with the robustness, spatial organisation and confinement of heterogeneous architectures. Despite rapid progress, the systems reported remain fragmented in terms of framework structures and heterogenisation strategies, which limits the identification of general structure–function relationships. This study reviews various representative systems, and critically compares heterogenisation strategies and their effects on catalytic performance. We also address conductive and photoelectrochemical architectures, multifunctional composites and emerging design strategies. We identify transferable design principles governing the transition from discrete molecular catalysts to spatially organised porous architectures. Although the Re-bpy CO2RR catalyst serves as a model platform, these principles offer more general guidance for the heterogenisation and functional integration of molecular catalysts in various catalytic transformations.
